subject: Security Education
sourceFile: Copy of National Value Education BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG (1).txt
examFormat: National Values Education (NVE) is a fusion of Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies; it assesses the development of Nigerian youth as responsible citizens, their moral, social, political and intellectual knowledge in nation-building, their ability to recognise the dimensions of human beings in different cultural and social contexts, and their level of security consciousness. Security Education is examined in Paper 1 of BECE National Values Education, which has sixty multiple-choice questions: 10 from Security Education and 50 from Civic Education.
excluded: Left out the syllabus.ng "About Us", "About BECE", eligibility, grading, registration, table of contents and FAQ chapters (publisher marketing / general information, not syllabus content). Civic Education and Social Studies themes are in their own files. The syllabus has only one Security Education sub-theme with five topics, so this file has five topics.
recommendedTexts: Comprehensive Studies on National Values for Junior Secondary School: Civic Education, Social Studies and Security Education — Meneka, Obiageli Augustina (Direct View Media)

topics.name: Common Crimes, Causes and Effects
objectives: Give examples of crime: falsehood, theft, rape, murder, advance fee fraud (419), sale of contaminated food, dealing in fake drugs etc.
Explain the causes and effects of common crimes
Describe crime prevention through cooperation with security agents, schools and neighbourhood authorities
topics.content: Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Observing and Reporting Common Crimes
objectives: Describe different ways of observing and reporting common crimes
topics.content: Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Common Crimes and Associated Punishments
objectives: Match common crimes with their associated punishments: theft (imprisonment), rape (imprisonment), drug trafficking (10 years imprisonment), human trafficking (5–10 years imprisonment), murder (death)
topics.content: Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Emergency Management
objectives: Explain the meaning of emergency management
Identify types of emergencies to be managed: accidents, fire, drowning, building collapse, food poisoning etc.
Describe the appropriate response in emergency management
topics.content: Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management. (The last listed type of emergency is cut off in the source after "Fake".)

topics.name: Crimes and National Security
objectives: Explain the meaning of national security
Identify crimes that affect national security: pipeline vandalisation, drug trafficking, human trafficking, illegal bunkering, terrorism, arson, importation of expired foods, drugs etc.
Demonstrate awareness of crimes that affect national security
topics.content: Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.
